basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Abscondit se, inquit, Adam et uxor ejus a facie Domini Dei in medio ligni paradisi. « Cum'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Abscondit se, inquit, Adam et uxor ejus a facie Domini Dei in medio ligni paradisi. « Cum Deus avertit intrinsecus faciem suam, non miremur haec fieri quae similia sunt dementiae, per nimium pudorem ac timorem, illo quoque occulto instinctu non quiescente, ut ea nescientes facerent, quae aliquid significent, quandoque scituris posteris propter quos ista conscripta sunt. Abscondunt se namque a facie Dei qui peccant, quia indignos se divinae pietatis reddunt aspectu. Abscondunt se a facie Dei, non ut ipsorum conscientiam internus arbiter non videat, sed ut ipsi gloriam vultus ejus nunquam nisi resipiscendo conspiciant. »
